paintings.title: The Policeman's Daughter
paintings.description: A famous painting depicting a swirling night sky over a quiet town.
paintings.authors_intention: To capture the emotional turmoil and complexity of human relationships.
paintings.context: No final da década de 1980, Paula Rego criou uma série de pinturas para explorar as relações familiares íntimas. Todas as relações parecem de certa forma disfuncionais, particularmente as que existem entre pais e filhas. A Filha do Policial está zangada, com a mão enfiada na bota do pai enquanto a limpa; um esboço para a pintura revela a sua génese numa relação um pouco mais inocente, uma menina mais nova, a acariciar a bota enquanto a limpa, com um castelo de brincar a simbolizar segurança aos seus pés. Na pintura, o castelo transformou-se num gato desconfiado, e a pose da menina, retirada de uma fotografia sexualmente explícita de Robert Mapplethorpe, é tudo menos inocente.

paintings.title: The Pesistence of Memory
paintings.description: A surreal painting featuring melting clocks draped over a barren landscape.
paintings.authors_intention: Dalí clarified that the soft watches were not inspired by physics, but by the camembert of time — specifically the sight of Camembert cheese melting in the sun.
paintings.context: The Persistence of Memory is one of Salvador Dalí's most famous works, created in 1931. The painting is a prime example of surrealism, a movement that sought to unlock the creative potential of the unconscious mind. The melting clocks are often interpreted as a symbol of the relativity of time and the fluidity of human perception. Dalí's intention was to challenge traditional notions of time and reality, inviting viewers to question their own perceptions and the nature of existence.

paintings.title: Guernica
paintings.description: A powerful political painting depicting the horrors of war, specifically the bombing of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War.
paintings.authors_intention: In the panel on which I am working, which I call Guernica, I clearly express my abhorrence of the military caste which has sunk Spain into an ocean of pain and death.
paintings.context: Guernica is a monumental painting created by Pablo Picasso in 1937. It was inspired by the bombing of the town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War. The painting is a powerful anti-war statement, depicting the suffering and chaos caused by the bombing. Picasso's intention was to raise awareness about the atrocities of war and to express his outrage at the violence inflicted upon innocent civilians. Guernica has since become an iconic symbol of the horrors of war and a testament to the resilience of the human spirit.

paintings.title: Nighthawks
paintings.description: A painting depicting people sitting in a diner late at night, evoking feelings of loneliness and isolation.
paintings.authors_intention: Unconsciously, probably, I was painting the loneliness of a large city.
paintings.context: Nighthawks is a famous painting by Edward Hopper, created in 1942. The painting captures a moment of quiet solitude in an urban setting, with three customers sitting in a brightly lit diner late at night. Hopper's intention was to convey the sense of isolation and loneliness that can be experienced in a bustling city. The painting has become an iconic representation of urban life and the human condition, resonating with viewers for its emotional depth and evocative atmosphere.
